sections.title: Financial Document Automation
sections.description: For JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and New York's financial institutions.

blocks.heading: Regulatory filing automation
paragraphs: AI for the enormous regulatory reporting burden of New York's financial institutions — automated compilation and validation of SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K exhibits), CFTC large trader reports, Federal Reserve bank call reports, and NYDFS quarterly reports. The regulatory reporting burden of a major New York bank involves hundreds of distinct filings annually — AI that extracts, aggregates, and formats financial data for these filings reduces the army of accountants and lawyers currently required.

blocks.heading: Trade documentation processing
paragraphs: AI processing the complex documentation of New York's trade finance and derivatives markets — ISDA master agreements, credit support annexes, confirmation documents, and the legal documentation of structured products and trade finance transactions.

blocks.heading: Know-Your-Customer (KYC) and onboarding automation
paragraphs: AI for the customer due diligence documentation that New York's regulated financial entities must complete — extracting beneficial ownership, sanctions screening, and adverse media monitoring from complex corporate organizational documents.

sections.title: Legal Operations Automation
sections.description: For Sullivan & Cromwell, Skadden, Davis Polk, Cravath, and New York's elite corporate law community.

blocks.heading: M&A due diligence automation
paragraphs: AI for New York's highly active M&A deal market — processing data room documents, extracting material contract provisions, regulatory filing history, IP ownership, and litigation exposure for the acquisition target due diligence that New York's BigLaw firms conduct at enormous volume.

blocks.heading: Contract review and abstraction automation
paragraphs: AI for the contract review programs at New York's large legal and corporate organizations — extracting key terms, obligations, and risk provisions from large contract portfolios for New York's in-house legal teams and outside counsel.

blocks.heading: Legal research memo automation
paragraphs: AI for the preliminary legal research and memo drafting that occupies significant junior attorney and paralegal time at New York's large firms.

sections.title: Healthcare Revenue Cycle Automation
sections.description: For NewYork-Presbyterian, Montefiore, NYU Langone, and NYC Health + Hospitals.

blocks.heading: New York Medicaid PA automation
paragraphs: AI for prior authorization assembly and submission for New York's massive and complex Medicaid program — Medicaid Managed Care organizations serving the state's large Medicaid population require PA automation that handles New York's specific managed care requirements, the MLTC (Managed Long-Term Care) prior authorization framework, and the Medicaid behavioral health carve-out's separate authorization requirements.

blocks.heading: Commercial payer PA automation
paragraphs: AI for prior authorization across New York's major commercial payers (Empire BlueCross BlueShield, UnitedHealth NY, Aetna NY, Cigna NY) for New York City's large academic medical centers.

blocks.heading: Clinical documentation improvement for NYC
paragraphs: AI identifying documentation gaps that affect DRG severity coding for New York's high-DRG-weight academic medical center inpatient populations.

sections.title: Insurance Operations Automation
sections.description: For AIG, MetLife, Chubb, and New York's world-leading insurance market.

blocks.heading: Commercial lines underwriting document processing
paragraphs: AI extracting structured risk information from commercial property and casualty submissions — the application, loss history, inspection reports, and supplemental data that commercial lines underwriters review to quote and bind coverage for AIG's and Chubb's large commercial books.

blocks.heading: Claims documentation automation
paragraphs: AI for NYDFS-regulated claims processing — organizing and extracting structured data from claims documentation, medical records, and expert reports for New York's large commercial and personal lines insurers.
